incident_summary_provided_by_client.location: Bartholomew's Pantry & Provisions, 2840 S. Mill Avenue, Tempe, AZ
incident_summary_provided_by_client.store_section: produce, just past the rotating display of stone fruit, near the citrus pyramid
incident_summary_provided_by_client.narrative: I was reaching for a bag of organic Cara Cara oranges when my right foot went out from under me. There was a puddle of what I later realized was leaked coconut water from a cracked carton — turquoise label, the Harmony Reef brand, the one in the carton not the can. I went down hard on my left hip and my right wrist when I tried to catch myself. I'm 63 and have osteoporosis, which my daughter keeps telling me I should warn places about but I don't think that's how it works. The store manager, a young man named Cassius, came over within maybe two minutes. He filled out an incident report on a tablet, asked me to sign with my finger, and gave me a paper copy. Report number is BPP-INC-2026-1147. He offered to call an ambulance but I asked my daughter to come get me instead.

content.client_message_body:
Dear Stockwell Heritage,

My daughter Anneliese said I should reach out to a lawyer because the store has been giving me the runaround for two weeks now. I broke my left hip — they put in three pins and a plate — and I fractured my right wrist (distal radius). I was in the hospital for four days and then in a skilled nursing facility for almost two weeks for rehabilitation. I am now home but I have a walker and a home health aide three times a week. My daughter took time off work to help me. I am a widow and live alone, so this has completely upended everything.

The store has called me twice. The first call was from a woman at their corporate office in Scottsdale, she said her name was something Patel, I think, and she offered to pay my deductible 'as a courtesy.' I said I'd think about it. Then yesterday a man called from Sentinel Crossroads Insurance, Harlan Eaglefeather, who said they handle Bartholomew's claims, and he wanted to take a recorded statement. I told him I needed to talk to my family first. He pressed me twice and I finally said no.

My medical bills so far are over $87,000 according to the statements I have stacked on my dining table, and I'm told I'll need more therapy and possibly a second surgery if the pins don't seat well. I'm on Medicare so a lot of it should be covered but there are bills coming from people I don't recognize.

I have not been back to the store. My daughter went last Saturday to try to look at the area but said it looked completely normal, nothing roped off, the display was different, no warning signs about wet floors anywhere.

I think I have a case but I don't know how this works. Please call me at the number above or email back. Mornings are best, I nap in the afternoons.

Sincerely,
Priscilla Eachus-Tomlinson

follow_up_email_thread.body: Mrs. Eachus-Tomlinson, thank you for reaching out. I'm so sorry for what you've been through. A few quick questions so we can evaluate this properly: (1) Can you tell me which hospital you were taken to, the surgeon who performed the procedure, the rehab facility, and the home health agency? We'll need to gather records from each. (2) Did you or anyone with you take any photographs at the scene — of the spill, the carton, the floor, the surrounding area, the produce section more broadly? Did you notice any other shoppers nearby who saw what happened, and did anyone give you their name or contact information? (3) Did you sign anything from the store beyond the incident report, and do you still have your paper copy? Please reply when you have a moment.

Hello, thank you for the quick reply. Let me try to answer.

The paper incident report I still have, it's on the dining table with the bills. The manager Cassius did not give me anything else to sign.

For your other questions, I have to be honest with you, I am not very good with this. When I fell I was so shocked and embarrassed that I didn't think to take any pictures. I had my phone in my purse and never got it out. My daughter wasn't there yet. I don't recall anyone else being in that aisle right when I went down, although I do remember a woman with a small child in a stroller came over after Cassius did, and an older gentleman in a Diamondbacks hat was standing at the end of the aisle but he just walked away. Cassius might have spoken to people, I don't know. Nobody gave me their name or a card or anything.

For the doctors, this is where I get embarrassed. I have a whole folder of papers but I genuinely couldn't tell you who is who. The surgeon spoke to me before the operation but I was on something for pain. The man who came every morning at the rehab place was very nice and had a beard but I don't remember his name either. My daughter would know some of this. The home health aide's name is Yuliana, that's all I know.

Is this enough to do something, or have I ruined it by not paying attention? I'm sorry. I should have been more on top of things.

Priscilla

content.specialist_internal_notes: High-value case potential — hip fracture with surgical fixation in a 63yo with osteoporosis, $87k+ medical so far, defendant insurer already attempted recorded statement (consciousness of liability). Liability theory turns on notice and reasonable inspection cycle at Bartholomew's Pantry; need to subpoena sweep logs, security footage, prior incident reports in produce section. Two material gaps before workup: (1) zero scene documentation from client — no photos, no witness contact info captured. We need to determine what store security footage exists (request preservation letter immediately, 30-day retention is typical), whether the manager Cassius identified any witnesses on the incident report, and whether the daughter Anneliese took any pictures during her later visit even casually. (2) client cannot identify any of her treating providers. We have the incident date and a vague description but no facility names, no surgeon name, no rehab facility, no home health agency beyond a first name. Cannot order records or build damages without provider IDs. Anneliese is the path — she was present, drove client home from hospital and rehab, and likely has discharge paperwork or knows the facility names. Request consent to contact her directly.
